entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen23518" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen23519" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen23519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23520" type="x-p"/> The psalmist, full of gratitude, purposes to praise God for ever, <reference osisRef="Psa.146.1">Psa 146:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Psa.146.2">Psa 146:2</reference>; and exhorts not to trust in man, not even the most powerful; for which he gives his reasons, <reference osisRef="Psa.146.3">Psa 146:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Psa.146.4">Psa 146:4</reference>. The great advantage of trusting in God, <reference osisRef="Psa.146.5">Psa 146:5</reference>. The mercies which they who trust in God may expect, <reference osisRef="Psa.146.6-Psa.146.9">Psa 146:6-9</reference>. The Divine government is everlasting, <reference osisRef="Psa.146.10">Psa 146:10</reference>. <div eID="gen23520" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23521" type="x-p"/> This is the first of the Psalms called Hallelujah Psalms, of which there are five, and which conclude the book. No author's name is prefixed to this, either in the Hebrew or Chaldee. But the Syriac, Vulgate, Septuagint, Ethiopic, and Arabic, attribute it to Haggai and Zechariah. It was probably written after the captivity, and may refer to the time when Cyrus, prejudiced by the enemies of the Jews, withdrew his order for the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem, to which revocation of the royal edict the third verse may refer: Put not your trust in princes etc.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen23521" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23522" type="x-p"/> While I live will I praise - The true feeling of a heart overpowered with a sense of God's goodness. <div eID="gen23522" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23523" type="x-p"/> While I have any being - בעודי beodi, in my continuance, in my progression, my eternal existence. This is very expressive.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen23523" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23524" type="x-p"/> Put not your trust in princes - This may refer, as has been stated above, to Cyrus, who had revoked his edict for the rebuilding of Jerusalem. Perhaps they had begun to suppose that they were about to owe their deliverance to the Persian king. God permitted this change in the disposition of the king, to teach them the vanity of confidence in men, and the necessity of trusting in himself.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen23524" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23525" type="x-p"/> His breath goeth forth - His existence depends merely, under God, on the air he breathes. When he ceases to respire he ceases to live; his body from that moment begins to claim its affinity to the earth; and all his thoughts, purposes, and projects, whether good or evil, come to nought and perish. He, then, who has no other dependence, must necessarily be miserable.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen23525" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23526" type="x-p"/> Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help - While he that trusts in man is miserable, he that trusts in God is happy. In the son of man, בן אדם ben Adam, there is no help, תשועה teshuah, no saving principle. Every son of Adam naturally comes into the world without this, and must continue so till the Lord open the eyes of the blind, <reference osisRef="Psa.146.8">Psa 146:8</reference>; but a measure of light is given from that true Light which lighteth every man that cometh into the world. This son of Adam returns to his earth, לאדמתו leadmatho, to the ground, from which he was taken; this refers directly to <reference osisRef="Gen.2.7">Gen 2:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.3.19">Gen 3:19</reference>. But he that has the God for his help who helped Jacob in his distress, and was with him, and sustained him in and through all adversities, can never be destitute; for this God changes not; he lives for ever, and his projects cannot perish. He has purposed that Israel shall be delivered from this captivity. Cyrus may change, but God will not; trust therefore in Him. He has all power; he made heaven and earth; he has them under his government and at his disposal; and should earth itself fail, heaven endures. And he keeps his truth for ever; and therefore his promises must be fulfilled to them that trust in him. Fear not.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen23526" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23527" type="x-p"/> Which ewecuteth judgment for the oppressed - For those who suffer by violence or calumny. This may refer to the Israelites, who suffered much by oppression from the Babylonians, and by calumny from the Samaritans, etc., who had prejudiced the king of Persia against them. <div eID="gen23527" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23528" type="x-p"/> Giving food to the hungry - No doubt he fed the poor captives by many displays of his peculiar providence. <div eID="gen23528" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23529" type="x-p"/> The Lord looseth the prisoners - And as he has sustained you so long under your captivity, so will he bring you out of it.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen23532" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23533" type="x-p"/> Preserveth the strangers - He has preserved you strangers in a strange land, where you have been in captivity for seventy years; and though in an enemy's country, he has provided for the widows and orphans as amply as if he had been in the promised land. <div eID="gen23533" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23534" type="x-p"/> The way of the wicked he turneth upside down - He subverts, turns aside. They shall not do all the wickedness they wish; they shall not do all that is in their power. In their career he will either stop them, turn them aside, or overturn them.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen23534" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23535" type="x-p"/> The Lord shall reign for ever - Therefore he can never fail; and he is thy God, O Zion.
